approved: Intellectual Property Laws Amendment (Productivity Commission Response Part 1 and Other Measures) Bill 2018

The Intellectual Property Laws Amendment (Productivity Commission Response Part 1 and Other Measures) Bill 2018 implements changes to Australia’s intellectual property laws based on Productivity Commission findings, including that patents grant exclusivity too readily, copyright is broader and longer than needed, and competition law should apply to IP transactions. Labor supported the bill and ongoing reform of IP laws.

The speaker supported the Intellectual Property Laws Amendment (Productivity Commission Response Part 1 and Other Measures) Bill 2018, which includes reforms to parallel import restrictions to protect intellectual property and royalty payments, amendments to plant breeder’s rights to encourage innovation, and an extension of the grace period from three to five years. The speaker also criticised the former Rudd government for failing to reform parallel importation of copyrighted books, arguing it protected commercial interests at the expense of consumers.

The Intellectual Property Laws Amendment (Productivity Commission Response Part 1 and Other Measures) Bill 2018 implements the Turnbull government's response to the Productivity Commission's IP review, reducing uncertainty for trademark importers, strengthening plant breeder protections, removing unused trademarks, and improving protections against unjustified threats. The Senate Economics Legislation Committee unanimously recommended the bill be passed on 22 June.
Intellectual Property Laws Amendment (Productivity Commission Response Part 1 and Other Measures) Act 2018
